findings.finding: NRC daily reactor status shows PSEG's fleet ran Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) with no refueling outage. Salem 1 and 2 never fell below 90%. Hope Creek ran at 83-88% for about three weeks (Aug 9-26), with one 70% day on Aug 8 and one 87% day on Jul 6. Peach Bottom 2 and 3 had only single-day dips (PB3 63% on Sep 5). In Q3 2025, by the company's own release, Power & Other operating earnings fell to $50M (from $69M) on 'higher nuclear related O&M from the Hope Creek refueling outage and fuel cycle extension work along with lower generation volume' (7.9 TWh). Add the PJM capacity price step-up from June 2026 ($329/MW-day on ~3,500 MW, against ~$270 the year before, from the Q2 deck), and Power has a y/y tailwind that could be worth about $0.04-0.10 a share. That supports a print at or a few cents above the $1.21-1.22 bar.

The one rise (+0.99, Nov 2025) came with a Q3 beat plus narrowing guidance to the upper half.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-30 (file current to 10/30/2026; Q3 rows read at offsets 100k-500k)
findings.why_not_priced: Outage calendars are known to analysts, so part of this is in the +8% y/y consensus. What is not public is the realised Q3 output: the company has not published it, and no preview cites it (Earnings Whispers only says the 92% Q2 capacity factor 'will be tested again'). If the clean run were priced, consensus would sit above the top of the y/y growth the company has shown. Q2 Power was +$31M y/y on a quarter that also had a Salem 2 outage, while the bar implies only ~$45M of total y/y growth.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 release (https://s24.q4cdn.com/601515617/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/PSEG-3Q-2025-Earnings-Release-Final-11-3-2025.pdf) gives the year-ago outage drag. Q2 2026 deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000788784/000119312526331660/d101695dex991.htm) gives capacity at $329/MW-day, >95% of 2026 output hedged, and the fall outages scheduled for Salem 1 and Peach Bottom 2, both Q4. Different documents, same direction. Being 95% hedged limits the energy-price upside, so the tailwind is volume and O&M, not price.

findings.finding: YTD operating EPS is $2.41 against a FY2026 guide of $4.28-$4.40. Consensus of $4.37 already sits near the top. Last year's Q3 release narrowed the guide to the upper half ($4.00-4.06 from $3.94-4.06), and the stock rose +0.99%, its only rise in 7 prints. The same move this year (to about $4.34-4.40) is likely but lands inside what the street already models. Only a raise above $4.40 would be news.

findings.finding: The Q3 call will be the first since PSEG said (2026-08-04) that PSE&G will file a base rate case by year-end 2026, three years ahead of its 2029 deadline. That filing comes while Governor Sherrill's EO1 utility business-model review runs: BPU Phase 2 explicitly lists authorized ROE and capital structure as levers, with its final report 'TBD (Early 2027)'. The July repeal of the 50bp transmission ROE adder costs about $40M a year (~$0.08) from 2027. Any request size, or 2027 commentary on the call, lands in a hostile NJ political setting where a large ask invites backlash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print that first announced the early rate case and kept guidance unchanged bought -0.46%. Earnings Whispers puts the post-print range at $66.15-$77.00, entirely below the prior quarter's $76-$83.70, and several targets were cut after it (Jefferies to $78, BMO to $79).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell to a 52-week low near $66.56 in September on this overhang. The specific request (revenue ask, ROE, rate design) and the 2027 bridge for the lost ROE adder are not yet public. If they were priced, previews would quote a requested ROE, and none does (Earnings Whispers: 'no timing, requested return, or rate design details').
findings.independence: Utility Dive 2026-08-05 (https://www.utilitydive.com/news/pseg-data-center-pjm-bilateral-contract-reliability/827045/) gives the ~$40M ROE adder hit and PSEG's 'encouraged' read of the Phase 1 report. That read is a counterweight: management framed the review as constructive (multiyear plans, performance-based rates), so the sign is uncertain and the size is kept small. This is an inference about call content, not a document number.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is less supportive than a month ago. The stock is up 9.06% in 20 days off its September 52-week low, a large move for a regulated utility with 22% realised vol. Short interest fell 30.8% between the Sep 30 and Oct 15 settlements (12.70M to 8.79M shares, 1.77% of float, 1.7 days to cover), so the covering bid that helped the rebound is largely spent. The stock goes into a print it has sold 6 of the last 7 times.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 1 up of 7, median absolute move 0.99%, max 2.19%. Every negative reaction was in a -0.14% to -2.19% band.
findings.why_not_priced: Run-up and short covering are by construction in the price. The claim is about asymmetry: with the cover done and a 9% bounce in hand, a good print has less fuel than a bad one has downside. That would be wrong if the run-up came from fresh long buying on a sector rotation, which I could not establish.
